title: Governor of Ohio

context.text: This is an open seat: Republican Gov. Mike DeWine is ineligible to seek a third consecutive term.

In the May 5, 2026 primary, Vivek Ramaswamy won the Republican nomination with 82.4% of the vote over Casey Putsch, and Amy Acton was unopposed for the Democratic nomination, receiving 767,360 votes. Don Kissick won the Libertarian primary with 97.8% of the vote over a write-in candidate.

Each nominee runs as a ticket with a lieutenant governor candidate: Ramaswamy with state Senate President Rob McColley, Acton with former Ohio Democratic Party chair David Pepper, and Kissick with James Mills. These three tickets are the only governor candidates certified for the general-election ballot in the Hamilton County Board of Elections list; other tickets appear only as write-ins.

candidates.name: Vivek Ramaswamy
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Rob McColley, president of the Ohio Senate. Won the May 5 Republican primary; endorsed by Donald Trump and the Ohio Republican Party.

priorities.text: Cutting the state income tax, eventually to zero, and immediately lowering property taxes, along with reducing government waste and regulation.
Educational reform, including universal school choice, a police officer in every school, tackling chronic absenteeism and merit-based pay for teachers and principals.
Law and order by empowering local police, and reattaching work requirements to Medicaid and welfare.

positions.summary: His campaign launch platform says his education plan includes universal school choice.

statements.quote: Phase out the state income tax—starting with eliminating capital gains taxes—so every Ohioan keeps more of what they earn.
Expand natural gas and deploy innovative energy technologies to strengthen Ohio’s energy supply and reduce electric bills for every family.

candidates.researchNotes: Plan page read 2026-10-19. No usable first-person statements found on abortion or guns (only secondary summaries). His plan-page line on 'backing the blue' by empowering police to make arrests is not about police funding or staffing, so it was not recorded.

candidates.name: Amy Acton
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate David Pepper, former chair of the Ohio Democratic Party. Unopposed in the May 5 Democratic primary.
candidates.currentRole: Former Director of the Ohio Department of Health (2019–2020)

priorities.text: Lowering costs for working families through her 'ActOn Lowering Costs' agenda, including child tax credits of $500 to $1,000 a year, a refundable credit for lower-income families and an Ohio Rx platform to reduce prescription-drug costs.
priorities.quote: As governor, my number one priority will be lowering costs for working families.

priorities.text: Easing enrollment in Medicaid, joining cities that have relieved residents' medical debt, and restoring energy-efficiency programs cut in House Bill 6.
A conditional moratorium on rapid data-center expansion, requiring companies to supply their own energy and build on former industrial sites rather than farmland.

positions.summary: Campaign issue page says she would protect access to abortion care as governor.
positions.quote: I will protect reproductive freedom so that every woman can access safe, legal abortion care, contraception, fertility treatments, and miscarriage care.

positions.summary: Campaign issue page calls for reforming the state voucher system and says public money should go to public schools.
positions.quote: Public money should be for public schools.

positions.summary: Campaign issue page says she would fully fund local law enforcement.
positions.quote: fully fund our local law enforcement

statements.quote: I'll lower energy bills for Ohioans by enhancing production and incorporating the lowest-cost and cleanest sources of energy.
statements.context: On her campaign issue page "Lowering Energy Costs"

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign issue pages read 2026-10-19. No statements found on guns, immigration or minimum wage. A health-coverage position that rested only on a news report's paraphrase of her affordability plan (Medicaid enrollment, medical debt) was removed.

candidates.name: Don Kissick
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate James Mills. Won the May 5 Libertarian primary with 97.8% of the vote.
candidates.researchNotes: Searched 2026-10-19; news coverage of his platform (e.g. certificate-of-need repeal, data-center moratorium) could not be loaded, and no campaign site was found, so nothing was added.

researchNotes: Running mates are noted in each candidate's ballotNote rather than as separate entries. Ballotpedia was not reachable (it blocks automated requests). The Ohio Secretary of State's own general-election certification page could not be loaded; the slate was checked against the Hamilton County Board of Elections certified list (Sept. 8, 2026) and the Wood County list (certified Aug. 26, 2026), which both print the three tickets (Acton/Pepper, Ramaswamy/McColley, Kissick/Mills) and list other tickets only as write-ins. Write-in tickets (e.g., Timothy Grady, Heather Hill, Renea Turner) are not included. No record items are listed for the two major candidates. No direct source on abortion or guns was found for either major candidate, so those positions are omitted. Little public material was found for Don Kissick beyond a short interview; his campaign site was not reachable. Hamilton County's certified list was re-read on Oct. 19 and matches the three tickets.
